quarterly_data.quarter: Advanced Energy Citi’s Global TMT Conference 2026 (09-10-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CAPACITY RAISED: THAILAND TAKES AE FROM OVER $3 BILLION TO OVER $5 BILLION OF CAPACITY BY 2028. CFO Paul Oldham: 'Today we have over $3 billion of capacity in our existing facilities... With Thailand coming on, that would give us over $5 billion of capacity as soon as 2028', which he tied to having 'sharpened our pencil a bit' and to accelerating investments (the earlier lower figure was the moderator's framing). CEO Steve Kelley said AE 'accelerate[d] the opening of our new factory in Thailand' in response to raised customer forecasts and is 'just opening a 500,000 sq ft facility, and we will be launching that facility with our largest customers, semiconductor, as well as our largest customers in data center.' Oldham said AE is 'spending roughly 2X the CapEx we would normally spend', which can return to 'a more normalized level of 3%-4%', and that the build was pulled forward out of the 2030 model because demand is running ahead.
quarterly_data.figure: over $3 billion of capacity today, over $5 billion as soon as 2028; 500,000 sq ft Thailand facility; capex running at roughly 2X normal versus a normalized 3%-4%

quarterly_data.quarter: Advanced Energy Citi’s Global TMT Conference 2026 (09-10-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: 800V TIMELINE PINNED: 2027 IS THE DESIGN-WIN YEAR, REVENUE IN 2028-2029. Kelley: 'we do not expect 800V to be significant from a revenue standpoint until 2028 at the earliest. So we think 2027 is a design win year for us, and 2028 and 2029 start to see revenue on 800V product.' AE is attacking it with a modular architecture - 'we have what we call a PDU, a power distribution unit. Think of it as a motherboard, essentially, where we could plug in these different 800V modules... 800V to six volts or to some other intermediate voltage' - explicitly because 'I do not think anybody knows exactly how the architecture is going to look a year or two from now.' He confirmed AE has solutions and active customer engagements for the AC/DC move out of the rack into a sidecar or power rack, and expects content per rack to rise as it has every generation. On cadence: 'every year a new solution is required. That is loosely tied to new introductions from Nvidia and other suppliers. The power requirements go up every year. But the space that we have to operate in does not change.'
quarterly_data.figure: 800V: 2027 design-win year, revenue 2028 and 2029, not significant until 2028 at the earliest

quarterly_data.quarter: Advanced Energy Citi’s Global TMT Conference 2026 (09-10-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: 2026 DATA CENTER GROWTH IS STILL ONE HYPERSCALER; THE 'SECOND WAVE' ONLY LANDS IN 2027-2029. Kelley: 'In 2026, what we have seen is a ramp based on our hyperscaler customer only. We have talked about a second wave customer set, but we do not see meaningful revenue from those customers until 2027 and 2028', with 2026 revenue coming from 2025 design wins ramping to volume at higher ASPs driven by higher power requirements. On the size of the second wave: 'in aggregate, we think the second wave customers could be as big as one of our hyperscale customers. We expect to reach that probably sometime in the 2028, 2029 timeframe.' Second-wave customers take standard products with minor modifications rather than the engineering-intensive customization hyperscalers require, so gross margin is similar but operating margin 'probably a bit better.'
quarterly_data.figure: second wave customers meaningful only in 2027 and 2028, reaching the size of one hyperscale customer in the 2028, 2029 timeframe

quarterly_data.quarter: Advanced Energy Citi’s Global TMT Conference 2026 (09-10-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: eVoS / eVerest / NavX ARE DESIGNED INTO SUB-2 NANOMETER LOGIC, BUT REVENUE IS A 2027-2028 EVENT. Kelley: 'Today we are being designed into sub-2 nanometer applications, logic for instance. We expect those products to become more meaningful from a revenue standpoint next year. We are already seeing shipments this year but, compared to the overall shipments we make, they are not that meaningful.' On the mix of what is ramping now: 'As you see the ramp this year, that is almost all older technologies. They are existing wins from many years ago where our customers are ramping the volume. I think as you move into 2027 and 2028, you will see a more significant percentage of the buy coming from new products, as those new processes ramp to volume.' He tied the pull to higher etch and dep intensity at fine geometries requiring higher power, multiple frequencies and more advanced metrology - capabilities that 'drive higher prices.'
quarterly_data.figure: new products (eVoS, eVerest, NavX) designed into sub-2 nanometer logic; meaningful revenue share only in 2027 and 2028

quarterly_data.quarter: Advanced Energy Citi’s Global TMT Conference 2026 (09-10-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: WFE CUSTOMERS HAVE TWO-YEAR VISIBILITY AND ARE GATED BY FAB SPACE, NOT ORDERS: Kelley said 'What we are being told by our customers is they have good visibility for the next two years. That is a lot of visibility. They are also telling us they are constrained by available fab basis. As their customers are able to accelerate the build-out schedule for new fabs for advanced memory and advanced logic, that is an upside for our customers, upside for us.' He said AE believes it is 'shipping to demand and not into inventory' because it is seen as a reliable supplier, so customers hold less buffer inventory, and that AE runs 'a just-in-time model with our largest customers. There's no lead time per se.'

quarterly_data.quarter: Advanced Energy Citi’s Global TMT Conference 2026 (09-10-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: NEW SOCKET - SYSTEM POWER INSIDE AI TEST AND BURN-IN: Kelley said that beyond the plasma-power heritage, 'over the past few years, we've put more emphasis on what we call our system power business... The demands have become increasingly complex, particularly as we move into the AI testing challenges. So we've had significant success there, getting our products designed into those testers, burn-in ovens, other applications where our customers need reliable system power.' On the trajectory: 'we haven't modeled exactly how it's going to grow, but what we know is we continue to expand capacity every quarter for these test applications', at margins 'similar to what we have in the plasma power business.'
